title: Algebraic K-Theory and Rigidity Conjectures for Discrete Groups
exact_target: For a torsion-free group $G$ and an integral domain $R$, are $0$ and $1$ the only idempotents of $RG$? Do the negative K-groups of $\mathbb{Z}G$, the reduced group $K_0(\mathbb{Z}G)$, and $\operatorname{Wh}(G)$ vanish? Are higher signatures homotopy invariant, closed aspherical manifolds topologically rigid, and groups of type FP of type FF? Is every finitely presented Poincaré-duality group of dimension at least five the fundamental group of an aspherical homology ANR-manifold? Is every hyperbolic group with boundary $S^n$ the fundamental group of a closed aspherical manifold? Are the Farrell–Jones assembly maps in algebraic K- and L-theory bijective?
